chunks: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the word of God, Mighty and Majestic: 'His Chair encompasses the heavens and the earth' — do the heavens and the earth encompass the Chair, or does the Chair encompass the heavens and the earth? So he said: 'Verily, everything is in the Chair.'

key_terms.الكرسي: The Kursi (Chair/Throne) — a divine reality mentioned in Ayat al-Kursi (2:255), understood in Shia tradition as encompassing all of creation
key_terms.عزّ وجلّ: Mighty and Majestic — an honorific for God (عَزَّ وَجَلَّ)
key_terms.وسع: To encompass, extend over, or contain — the verb used in the Quranic verse about the Kursi's scope

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Sadiq say about the meaning of the Kursi in Ayat al-Kursi?
ai.summary: Zurara ibn A'yan posed to Imam Sadiq (AS) a profound cosmological question inspired by Ayat al-Kursi (2:255): is the divine Kursi (Chair/Throne) greater than the heavens and earth, or vice versa? The Imam responded decisively that everything — all of creation — is contained within the Kursi. This teaching establishes the infinite encompassing nature of the divine Throne, which in Shia theological tradition represents the totality of God's knowledge and dominion over creation.
